[[305.1]] 96. DAMARIS LADY MASHAM AN LEIBNIZ

[[305.2]] Oates, 24. November (5. Dezember) 1704. [91.105.]

[[305.13]] S^#'r Oates 24 Novbr. 1704.

[[305.14]] It being a long while since the date of your First Letter to me, thō not very long since I

[[305.15]] receiv'd it; the High value that I have for the Honour of your Correspondence makes me fear

[[305.16]] incuring the suspicion of a neglect I can never be Guiltie of in your regard; and induces me now

[[305.17]] to write, thō the loss I have but lately had; and since That the solicitous Care which attends the

[[305.18]] first sending an onely Child into the world under his own Conduct, dos at present much

[[305.19]] indispose me.

[[305.20]] Yours of the 16^#'t^#'h of Sept^#'b^#'r came not to my Hands till our 31 of October: the day wherin

[[305.21]] was Perform'd the last office to one that had been my Freind above half my life time. M^#'r Locke

[[305.22]] I meane. A Freind who thō very Accidentally an Acquaintance and Perfectly unknown to my

[[305.23]] Familie, has supplyd to me the Plan of a Father, and Brother: and to whose Direction, next to

[[305.24]] the Favour of God, I cheifly ascribe it if my Son (as I have reason to Hope) be Bless'd with a

[[305.25]] Sound Mind in a Sound Body. But This has been but the Best Effect of M^#'r Locks Freindship,

[[305.26]] not the onely one: for he has in his last Will left to my Son (or in case of his Death to myself) a

[[305.27]] legacie in money of a value seldom givn by Any to such as are no way related: with other Gifts

[[305.28]] to him amongs which is the division of his Librarie betwixt him, and his Kinsman and Executor

[[305.29]] M^#'r Peter King; a man of great Worth on many Accounts; and Particularly as a member of

[[305.30]] Parliament (wherin no one is Beleev'd more immoveably True to the Protestant Interest).

[[306.1]] In telling you thise Obligations which I have had to M^#'r Locke, I shall, I hope, make my

[[306.2]] excuse, if the Tribute which I pay of a well Merited Affection to the Memorie of this

[[306.3]] Extraordinarie Freind, as well as Extraordinarie Man, unfits me yet for other Thought than such

[[306.4]] as the Heart Dictates.

[[306.5]] Your 2^#'d Letter came to my Hands but two days since. I have no remembrance of it at

[[306.6]] present if M^#'r Locke has ever explain'd to me his Thoughts concerning the Production of Matter.

[[306.7]] That This is less Inconceivable than the Creation of an Immaterial Substance was what I

[[306.8]] imagin'd before I knew M^#'r Locke, which has made me, perhaps, more inadvertant than I should

[[306.9]] else have been to what he intimates in the Chapter you cite.

[[306.10]] Not long since, the Library Keeper of the Universitie of Oxford desir'd of M^#'r Locke, for

[[306.11]] the Bodleian Library, the Books of which he was the Author.

[[306.12]] M^#'r Locke in return to this request, Presented to the said Library All the Books Publish'd

[[306.13]] under his Name.

[[306.14]] But in a Codicil to his Will he takes Notice That he had not been herein understood fully

[[306.15]] to have answer'd the request made him; it being suppos'd he was the Author of other Treatises

[[306.16]] to which his Name was not prefix'd. In Complyance therefore, he says, with what was

[[306.17]] desir'd, in the utmost extent of it, and in acknowledgment of the Honour done

[[306.18]] him in thinking his Writings Worthy to be plac'd amongst the Works of the

[[306.19]] Learned, in that August Repositorie; he dos further give to the Publick Library

[[306.20]] of the Universitie of Oxford these following Books, which are;

[[306.21]] Three letters Concerning Tolleration.

[[306.22]] Two Treatises of Goverment.

[[306.23]] The Reasonableness of Christianitie as deliver'd in the Scriptures.

[[307.1]] A Vindication of the Reasonableness etc. from M^#'r Edwards Reflections.

[[307.2]] A 2d Vindication of the Reasonableness of Christianitie.

[[307.3]] These he says are All the Books whereof he was the Author, Publish'd

[[307.4]] without his Name. and many other Anonymous Books besides These, haveing been Attribut'd

[[307.5]] to M^#'r Locke. I thought you Might not be Unwilling to know what he truely did Write, and

[[307.6]] what was not His; which has made me Transcribe this so Solemn a Declaration. If you have

[[307.7]] read the Reasonableness of Christianitie as deliverd in the Scriptures. I should be very glad to

[[307.8]] know your Thoughts of it. If you have not seen this Book, I desire to Present you with it. It was

[[307.9]] long ago Translated into French by a Person whom I have been Happy in haveing for

[[307.10]] Praeceptor to my Son. Mons^#'r Coste, the Translator of M^#'r Lockes Essay.

[[307.11]] I am much oblig'd to you S^#'r for your good Wishes. They will always be a Pleasure to, and

[[307.12]] always return'd by

[[307.13]] Your Most Humble Servant Da Masham.
